question: What is the primary digital equivalent of a patient's traditional paper chart called?
explanation: An Electronic Medical Record serves as the direct digital replacement for standard paper clinical charts. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T9#GNS212_U4_T9_h1)

question: How do EMRs primarily improve upon traditional paper-based health record systems in busy clinics?

options.A: By offering faster data retrieval and less physical storage
options.B: By automatically diagnosing complex patient diseases without testing
options.C: By completely eliminating the need for any clinical documentation
options.D: By removing all requirements for patient data privacy protection

explanation: Digital records clear up physical filing space while allowing instant access to patient histories. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T9#GNS212_U4_T9_h1)

question: Which EMR component alerts clinicians to potential drug allergies during prescription entry?
explanation: Clinical decision support tools warn staff about safety issues like allergies or dangerous drug interactions. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T9#GNS212_U4_T9_h2)

question: What is the main purpose of an audit trail inside an EMR system?

options.C: Tracking who accessed or edited patient files

explanation: Audit trails record every interaction with a file to maintain security and accountability. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T9#GNS212_U4_T9_h2)

question: What common nursing documentation problem is instantly solved by switching to typed EMR entries?
explanation: Typed entries remove ambiguities caused by messy handwriting, reducing clinical errors. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T9#GNS212_U4_T9_h3)

question: A nurse uses barcode scanning on a patient wristband before drug administration to achieve what goal?

options.A: Updating the hospital staff attendance register
options.B: Recording daily ward temperature and humidity
options.C: Confirming the correct patient and medication match
options.D: Submitting the patient bill directly to the pharmacy

explanation: Barcode scanning verifies identity and prescription details right at the bedside to prevent administration errors. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T9#GNS212_U4_T9_h3)

question: Which infrastructure issue frequently threatens EMR usability in many Nigerian hospitals?
explanation: Frequent power outages interrupt digital record access, requiring reliable backup generators. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T9#GNS212_U4_T9_h4)

question: Why does unexpected EMR system downtime create clinical risks for nursing staff?

options.A: It prevents nurses from administering any oral medications
options.B: It forces a temporary return to paper records, risking documentation gaps
options.C: It deletes all historical patient records permanently
options.D: It automatically discharges all stable patients from the ward

explanation: Downtime disrupts normal workflow and can lead to missing or delayed documentation. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T9#GNS212_U4_T9_h4)

question: What security practice ensures staff only view patient records relevant to their assigned duties?
explanation: Role-based access restricts file viewing to ensure staff only access data needed for their work. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T9#GNS212_U4_T9_h5)

question: Why is sharing personal EMR login credentials with a colleague a dangerous practice?

options.A: It compromises accountability and violates patient data confidentiality
options.B: It automatically shuts down the main hospital computer network
options.C: It doubles the internet data usage charges for the ward
options.D: It deletes all previous nursing entries in the system

explanation: Shared logins break audit trails and expose private health records to unauthorized eyes. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T9#GNS212_U4_T9_h5)

question: How do legal systems view digital EMR documentation compared to paper charting?

options.A: As unofficial notes with no legal importance
options.B: With the exact same legal weight and validity
options.C: As property of the software vendor only
options.D: As temporary drafts that expire after one week

explanation: Electronic health records are legally binding documents accepted in courts of law. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T9#GNS212_U4_T9_h6)

question: What is the correct action when a nurse forgets to document a care intervention and must add it later?

options.A: Leave the care undocumented to avoid any potential audit trail flags
options.B: Record the note as a late entry with the correct current timestamp
options.C: Ask a colleague to backdate the entry using their administrator login
options.D: Change the system clock to match the time the care actually occurred

explanation: Late entries must reflect the true time they were added while noting when the event took place. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T9#GNS212_U4_T9_h6)
